reader_summary.headline: Acquired explains how Disney saved its animation studio and built an entertainment empire.
reader_summary.overview: In the 1980s, Disney faced financial trouble and hired Michael Eisner and Frank Wells to fix its struggling animation division. The new leaders focused on great stories, raised ticket prices, and used new technology to create profitable films. They also expanded into parks, retail, and media networks, transforming the company into a massive global brand.

key_points.text: Disney raised ticket prices and released movies on home video to create huge profits for new projects.
key_points.evidence_quote: One of the first things they do that ends up, I think, really setting up all the following success that Eisner and Wells and Katzenberg have is they raise the ticket prices at Disneyland and Disney World.

key_points.text: The company bought ABC and ESPN, using sports cash flow to fund parks and other entertainment ventures.
key_points.evidence_quote: This is how they funded it all, was all the cash that ESPN and the cable networks, but mostly ESPN, were spitting out.

key_points.text: After 9/11, shareholder support for Michael Eisner collapsed, leading to his eventual removal from the CEO role.
key_points.evidence_quote: Roy E. Disney announces that he is resigning from the Disney Board of Directors, citing, quote, serious differences of opinion about the direction and style of management.

thesis: The episode argues that Bob Iger's leadership was pivotal in reviving Disney Animation and that the company remains uniquely positioned to produce high-quality branded content. It further asserts that ESPN served as a critical financial engine, providing a 'pseudo-infinite wellspring of capital' to fund the broader Disney empire, which contributed to Michael Eisner's success as a CEO.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that the Disney stock jumped in response to the board's decision to remove Michael Eisner as chairman.
claims.quote: They announced this. The Disney stock jumps in response. Meanwhile, Comcast stock has been falling. So a few weeks later, Comcast formally withdraws their bid.

claims.claim: The speaker states that Bob Iger's campaign framing was brilliant and that he was the only one positioned to revive Disney Animation.
claims.quote: And he actually hires a political campaign consultant to help him with this. And he realizes that, okay, I am the number two to an unpopular incumbent. I'm the vice president of a massively unpopular president right now who has just become a lame duck.

claims.claim: The speaker asserts that Disney is still the best positioned company to create high-quality branded content despite past problems.
claims.quote: And still nobody is better positioned than Disney to do that, even despite all the problems and distractions and the downfall of animation over the last 10 years, it's still Disney.

claims.claim: The speaker highlights that ESPN provided a pseudo-infinite wellspring of capital to fund everything else at Disney.
claims.quote: And it's worth it because buying ESPN was this pseudo-infinite wellspring of capital to fund everything else. But it cost the clarity.

claims.claim: The speaker lists ESPN, the flywheel business, and the Disney Renaissance as the top reasons Michael Eisner was a great CEO.
claims.quote: And also Disney's Renaissance, but like, I'd put that at four, below ESPN, ESPN, and ESPN.
